purpose: P1 scenario coverage for LFNST / primary-transform overlap. Target state entry is verified separately from data correctness; a scenario that never enters its target state is a failure.

tool.compile: vlog -sv per file, one module per invocation, work library rebuilt each run

tb.location: work_endattr/ (staging, not yet committed to repo)
tb.stimulus_style: port-driven; internal state observed only to confirm target-state entry

tu_vectors.source: computed by validate_gate_c_model (inverse_2d + output_beats SAT10), not hand-written

cases.name: two_lfnst_back_to_back
cases.target_state: queue depth 2 occupied while two LFNST TUs are in flight

cases.name: lfnst_then_plain_descriptor_during_lfnst
cases.target_state: descriptor accepted in the same cycle window as an active LFNST phase

cases.name: plain_then_lfnst
cases.target_state: LFNST TU accepted while the primary kernel is running

cases.name: lfnst_overlap_with_output_stall
cases.target_state: LFNST overlap plus genuine output backpressure

negative_controls.name: compute_priority_swap
negative_controls.mutation: compute arbitration prefers slot1 over slot0
negative_controls.interpretation: P1 scenarios never have both slots READY in the same window, so the fixed slot0 priority is not exercised here; that ordering is covered by the existing S03 case, not by P1. Recorded as a limitation, not as a pass.

negative_controls.name: lfnst_set_index_dropped
negative_controls.interpretation: S06 still passes because its LFNST TU uses set0, so forcing 0 is a no-op there; that is expected and shows the check is data-dependent rather than unconditional.

findings.statement: kernel_run_q and lfnst_run_q never overlap in any P1 scenario (0 cycles). The single compute arbiter admits one owner at a time, so simultaneous primary-transform and LFNST execution is structurally unreachable, not merely untested.
it_data_out_vld = output_active && it_data_out_req (unified_its_wrapper.sv:1678). The output handshake is req-gated: vld is a transfer qualifier, not an availability indicator.
findings.evidence: During 1047 stall cycles with req low, vld stayed low, the word stayed stable and done stayed deasserted; no beat was lost across the stall.
findings.risk: A downstream that asserts it_data_out_req only after seeing it_data_out_vld would never see any output. The existing protocol TB codifies the req-gated reading (its_unified_submission_top_protocol_tb.sv:45-50 fatal 'pending stall violation'), but no repository document states the semantics, so the externally visible contract is undocumented.
findings.recommendation: Add the handshake semantics to the interface clarification list (Q-item) and state it explicitly in the submission interface description.
